title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for carpet and upholstery cleaning
audience: Owners of carpet and upholstery cleaning businesses, including solo operators, who quote per room, per item and per job for homes and small offices.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer for carpet
instruction.body: 'Carpet clean, $25 a room' is a price, not an offer. 'Steam clean of the listed rooms and two dining chairs, with a stain check before work, a stated dry time and a return visit for any listed stain that does not lift' is an offer. The client buys a known result and certainty about what is included. Do not promise that every stain will be removed, because some stains may not lift.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a carpet offer
instruction.body: Set the outcome (the listed rooms and items, cleaned by the method named), the time frame (on-site time and the dry time you set), what the client must do (move furniture, clear the floor, secure pets, report stains and existing damage before work), the certainty you give (a room and item list, photos of stains before work) and the risk you carry (a return visit for listed items). A written quote becomes binding once accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). WA guidance says a quote should set out the job, possible extra costs, materials, labour and time to finish (WA only).

instruction.heading: Tiers, and each item on its own line
instruction.body: Use a basic tier (one method, listed rooms), a standard tier (a method upgrade or a treatment) and a whole-home tier. Put each upholstery item on its own line, because directory prices are set per item. A low per-room offer often means a basic one-step process: Yellow Pages warns that offers as low as $10 a room can be basic (9 January 2025, updated November 2025). Say which method each price covers.

instruction.heading: Show one total, and price extra work first
instruction.body: Show one total including GST and say whether GST is included (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024; WA guidance for WA). If you find extra work, price it in writing and get permission before you do it. Business Queensland suggests charging additional costs at cost plus a stated percentage, and it suggests 15 per cent. That is a suggestion, not a benchmark (16 November 2022).

instruction.heading: Deposit and guarantee
instruction.body: If you take a deposit, WA guidance says it should generally be no more than 10 per cent of the price, and payments should follow completed stages (WA only; 4 September 2026). Offer a return visit for listed stains you cannot lift. Under the consumer guarantees a business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria's guidance, 13 October 2023; a Victorian page, so check your state's consumer agency). That page sets no fix window.

procedure: Write the result in one sentence a client would repeat, for the listed rooms and items.
Ask about stains, pets and existing damage, and record them before you quote.
Measure the rooms and count the upholstery items, and list each as its own line.
State the method for each price, and say what a lower price leaves out.
Price from timed work and your costs, then show one total with GST stated.
Write the exclusions, the dry time you can deliver, the client's inputs and the validity date.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A solo cleaner is quoting a three-bedroom home with four rooms of carpet and two dining chairs for a steam clean. The client has read that carpet cleaning costs about $55 a room.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the quote need to show, and what range can the cleaner cite?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cleaner writes each room and each chair as its own line. Yellow Pages gives a steam range of $25 to $45 per room (9 January 2025, vendor directory). Four rooms at the top of that range is $180, and two dining chairs at $15 to $30 each is $30 to $60. The total is about $210 to $240 (CALC), before travel and any minimum charge, which the source does not give. The $55 average is a directory figure, so the cleaner checks it against the minutes the rooms really take rather than quoting it. The quote states the method, the dry time, the stain notes and the exclusions. It does not quote the cheapest offer in the directory.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a low per-room price without stating the method.
commonErrors.prevention: State the method and steps, and say what a lower price leaves out.

commonErrors.error: Leaving upholstery out of the quote.
commonErrors.prevention: List each item as its own line with its own price.

commonErrors.error: Promising that stains will be removed.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the method and note the stains that may not lift.

commonErrors.error: Treating a directory range as your minimum charge.
commonErrors.prevention: Set your own minimum. The research did not find a carpet minimum charge.

commonErrors.error: Claiming a cleaning result you cannot show.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you can show, and describe the process you use.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant a licence, registration or insurance. Licence and insurance rules for carpet and upholstery cleaning were not researched, so check the rules for your state or territory.
Price display: show the total including GST (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024). WA guidance on quotes and deposits applies in Western Australia only.

The Comcare page read for this lesson covers bathroom cleaning products. It supports the principle of keeping safety data sheets and following label directions, but it does not set rules for carpet solutions.
Wastewater disposal and solution rules for carpet and upholstery cleaning were not researched. Check your local council's rules and each product label before use.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Quote carpet and upholstery as listed rooms and items, each on its own line, with the method stated.
Show one total including GST, and price extra work in writing before you do it.
Gaps: no government or trade-body carpet price, minimum charge, strata or agent channel, or wastewater rule was found.

knowledgeChecks.question: What makes a carpet quote clear to a client?
options: A single low per-room price with no method stated
Each room and item on its own line, with the method and exclusions
A promise that every stain will be removed

knowledgeChecks.question: A client offers to pay $10 a room for a steam clean. What should you check first?
options: Whether the lower price covers the same method and steps as your quote
Whether the client has a large house
Whether the room count is an even number

knowledgeChecks.question: Extra work is found after the quote. What should happen?
options: Do it straight away and bill it at the end
Price it in writing and get the client's permission before doing it
Skip it and hope the client does not notice

sourceReferences: Yellow Pages Australia, 'Carpet cleaning costs', https://www.yellowpages.com.au/articles/home-cleaning/carpet-cleaning-costs, published 9 January 2025, updated November 2025. Vendor directory. Supports: per-room, whole-home and upholstery price ranges, and a warning that offers as low as $10 a room may be a basic one-step process.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Ask us: Estimates and quotes', https://consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/publications/ask-us-estimates-and-quotes, last updated 18 November 2024. Western Australia only. Supports: a quote is a fixed price and an estimate can move; extra work needs the customer's permission; a written quote should state the job, possible extra costs, materials, labour and time to finish.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Estimates, quotes and deposits', https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/estimates-quotes-and-deposits, last updated 4 September 2026. Western Australia only. Supports: show the total including GST and say whether GST is included; a deposit should generally be no more than 10 per cent; extra work needs written approval.

business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted; a quote should recover cost plus a margin.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Queensland. Supports: list add-ons and alternatives on the quote; charge extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage (the source suggests 15 per cent, which is not a benchmark); follow up 7 to 14 days after the quote; confirm scope, capacity and deadline before quoting.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Victoria. Supports: a business should be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge; the page sets no fix-window length.

Comcare, 'Bathroom cleaning products', https://www.comcare.gov.au/office-safety-tool/spaces/bathrooms/bathroom-cleaning-products, no date shown. Supports: obtain the safety data sheet (SDS) for each product, keep original labels, use the PPE the SDS specifies, and follow label directions. The page covers bathroom products only.
business.gov.au, 'Display prices', https://business.gov.au/legal/fair-trading/display-prices, page metadata 18 January 2024. Supports: displayed prices should show the total price, including GST.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

Notes: the $210 to $240 total is arithmetic (CALC) on the directory's per-room and per-item ranges. The $55 average and $10 offer are directory figures. The 15 per cent is a suggestion from Business Queensland. The Comcare page covers bathroom products only.
